name: GE GUD27 Electric Dryer Heater Element
purpose: GUD27 §34 — outer element and combined inner elements each 23.7–26 Ω at 240 VAC (~9 A each).
failureModes: Open element — no heat; verify safety, inlet, outlet, and high-limit thermostats in series
testingTips: Disconnect leads at heater assembly; drum removal required per wiring diagram p.77
Inner elements wired in parallel — measure combined inner path per diagram
Biased thermostats must be cool for continuity checks at heater

name: GE GUD27 Dryer Motor Start Winding
purpose: GUD27 §30 — start winding M6 to M4 at motor terminals.
failureModes: Open start winding — motor hums, no tumble
Overload protector open — reads OL at run winding path
testingTips: Read start winding at motor M6–M4 with harness disconnected
Run winding: terminal 2 on start switch to NO on door switch

name: GE GUD27 Dryer Motor Run Winding
purpose: GUD27 §30 — run winding from terminal 2 on start switch to NO terminal on door switch.
failureModes: Open run winding or overload — no tumble
Centrifugal switch M1–M2 not closing — no heat on gas/electric heat path
testingTips: Door closed for run-winding path through door switch NO
Motor overload is internal — OL indicates motor replacement

name: GE GUD27 Dryer Timer Motor
failureModes: Open timer motor — timer will not advance on timed cycles
Timer motor OK but no advance on auto — check outlet thermostat and 4500 Ω advance resistor (electric)
testingTips: Disconnect timer wiring before bench measurement
Timer is intentionally ungrounded — disconnect power before access

name: GE GUD27 Timer Voltage-Dropping Resistor
purpose: GUD27 §25 — 4500 Ω resistor in series with timer motor on electric models; check timer contacts A to T in Off/Cool Down.
failureModes: Open resistor — auto cycle timer stalls in heat portion
Resistor OK but no advance — outlet thermostat not opening or vent restriction
testingTips: Electric models only — resistor on control bracket with timer
Measure A to T with timer in Off or Cool Down position per service guide

name: GE GUD27 Gas Dryer Ignitor
purpose: GUD27 §39 — glo-bar ignitor approximately 40–400 Ω; max 4 A when energized.
failureModes: Open ignitor — no ignition, no heat
Ignitor glows but no flame — flame detector or gas valve coils
testingTips: Remove burner assembly to access ignitor on gas valve bracket

name: GE GUD27 Gas Valve Safety + Booster Coils
purpose: GUD27 §40 — safety coil ~1400 Ω + booster coil ~580 Ω in series path to open safety valve.
failureModes: Open safety/booster path — ignitor glows, no gas release
Safety holds open alone once energized — test both coils
testingTips: Disconnect coil harness at gas valve
Both safety and booster coils required to open safety valve initially

name: GE GUD27 Gas Valve Main Coil
purpose: GUD27 §40 — main valve coil approximately 1300 Ω; bypassed by N.C. flame detector until heated.
failureModes: Open main coil — flame lights briefly then shuts off
Flame detector stuck open — main coil never energizes properly
testingTips: Flame detector must be cool/closed for bench coil readings
Short burn ~1–2 min then valve closes — suspect flame detector or weak coils

name: GE GUD27 Long-Vent Blower Motor
purpose: GUD27 §33 — long-vent blower motor in parallel with drive motor, approximately 14.25–15.75 Ω.
failureModes: Open blower motor — poor airflow on long-vent models, long dry times
Motor OK but poor venting — inspect duct restriction
testingTips: Long-vent models only — blower motor parallel to drive motor
Rotate drive motor to access blower motor removal
